title: Saga Pattern
text: Let's explore advanced transaction processing with a focus on specialized transaction models. Today we'll be diving into the Saga pattern. It is an important concept in managing transactions across multiple services. So what exactly is the Saga pattern? A Saga is a sequence of local transactions. Each transaction updates data within a single service. Think of it as a series of steps where each step performs an action in one place

For instance, an order Saga orchestrator class might execute the Saga by creating an order, processing payment, reserving inventory and shipping the order

text: . If any step fails, the orchestrator compensates by canceling the shipment and releasing the inventory. This centralized approach provides a clear and controlled way to manage complex transactions. The Saga pattern offers several benefits, including scalability, because there is no need for distributed locks. It also ensures resilience, as it can handle service failures gracefully.
